transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess what finally made me come in is that I’ve been having a really hard time keeping up with basic adult stuff. Like, I mean, things I feel like I should be able to handle—paying bills on time, replying to interview emails, remembering appointments, finishing errands I said I’d do.

It’s not that I don’t care. I really do. But I keep forgetting or putting things off and then it’s suddenly too late, and it’s started actually costing me opportunities. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, because it sounds irresponsible, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should talk to someone.
Looking back to when you were a child, did you already have this kind of trouble staying organized and following through on things?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did okay in school, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything. But even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright, but I was always losing worksheets or couldn’t find assignments in my desk.

I remember my desk being kind of… a disaster, honestly. And I’d rush through directions or miss parts of them, and I got told I talked out of turn. It wasn’t like I was trying to be difficult—I just seemed to always be a little scattered. Does that count as the kind of thing you mean?
Do these kinds of problems happen in most parts of your life, not just with school or work?

Yeah… unfortunately, it’s not just school or work. I wish it were more contained than that.

Since I got fired, it’s kind of shown up everywhere. I’ve missed follow-up emails for interviews, even when I really wanted the job, and then I feel awful because it looks like I don’t care. I also had to step back from a volunteer project I actually cared about because I couldn’t keep up with the basic communication and tasks.

So… I’m not working right now, and I feel like I can’t reliably manage the steps I need to move my life forward. That sounds dramatic, maybe, but that’s how it feels. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Um… I don’t know if I’d call it excessive worry, exactly. I mean, I worry when I’ve missed something or when there’s a real consequence, but I’m not sure I’m constantly worrying about lots of different things out of nowhere.

Maybe I’m not explaining that well. It feels more like I get overwhelmed once things are already messy, rather than sitting around imagining disasters all the time. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I’m… not sure I’d say depressed most days. I mean, I’ve definitely felt discouraged and pretty bad about how things are going, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being depressed.

I don’t want to overstate it. It feels more like I get upset with myself when I can’t keep up, if that makes sense. But “down most days” — I’m not sure. How would you define that?
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.

I mean, I’ll have thoughts about things I forgot or stuff I need to fix, and they can kind of nag at me, but I don’t usually have, like, random unwanted thoughts that feel intrusive or that I’m trying to push out over and over.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean — is that what you’re asking about?
Do you tend to be such a perfectionist that it makes it hard for you to finish tasks?

I don’t think perfectionism is the main thing, no. I mean, I can get picky about wanting something to be good, but I don’t usually feel like it has to be perfect before I can finish it.

If anything, I’m not totally sure how to separate that from just… having trouble getting through things sometimes. But I wouldn’t want to say I’m such a perfectionist that it stops me, unless I’m missing what you mean.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood across multiple settings, with clear functional impairment. Symptoms include disorganization, losing materials, missing parts of instructions, forgetfulness, failure to follow through, and difficulty managing tasks and communications. Interview responses do not support generalized anxiety, depressive disorder, OCD, or perfectionism-driven avoidance as primary explanations.
